Smartwatch blood pressure monitoring was okay. AI is making it better.

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1023 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that when the United States Food and Drug Administration cleared the Apple Watch’s Hypertension Notification Feature last year, some saw it as a turning point in the fight against one of the leading causes of cardiac disease.
  • While that sounds great, the reality of smartwatch hypertension tools is more nuanced.
  • Sources indicate that that context is worth keeping in mind when considering new research from scientists at Google and a clinical partner from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Harvard Medical School recently published in the journal Nature.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that when the United States Food and Drug Administration cleared the Apple Watch’s Hypertension Notification Feature last year, some saw it as a turning point in the fight against one of the leading causes of cardiac disease. Rather than booking a doctor’s appointment and strapping a bulging cuff around one’s arm, users could instead receive passive hypertension alerts from the watch’s optical sensors to track blood flow patterns. Watch wearers who were previously unaware that they had signs of this ever-common “silent killer” would receive an alert advising them to seek out a clinician. Early intervention could mean a better chance at beginning life-saving interventions.

While that sounds great, the reality of smartwatch hypertension tools is more nuanced. Apple’s own validation data highlighted that their feature would miss around 59 percent of people with undiagnosed high blood pressure. Newer United States population level research from the University of Utah and the University of Pennsylvania went a step further, and warned that the absence of an alert could give wearers a false sense of security, potentially making them less likely to go get a proper cuff screening. The feature, in other words, isn’t necessarily harmful, but it also isn’t a medical silver bullet.

Sources indicate that that context is worth keeping in mind when considering new research from scientists at Google and a clinical partner from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Harvard Medical School recently published in the journal Nature. The team claims they created a new AI system that pairs with a consumer smartwatch to passively detect signs of high blood pressure, “with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure devices.”.

The newly introduced system draws on two sensors already found in many consumer smartwatches: an optical pulse sensor (which tracks changes in blood volume at the wrist) and an accelerometer. An AI algorithm then analyzes several days of  readings, factors in the wearer’s height, and then calculates the probability that they have hypertension.

Recent findings suggest that google’s system builds on Apple’s approach by adding in the watch’s accelerometer to the mix, which can pick up the faint wrist vibrations of each heartbeat. The results look promising. In initial screenings, the combined system caught more cases of high blood pressure than a standard office cuff reading, though it still missed about a third of cases. And while the researchers involved still advise against using the tool as a substitute for seeing a doctor, it’s potentially another step forward in attempts to use common wearable tech to catch underlying signs of disease earlier.

“By gently prompting at-risk individuals to step into a clinic for formal assessment, this technology holds the potential to significantly close the global awareness gap and catch hypertension before it causes permanent cardiovascular damage,” Google researchers note in a blog post.

Recent findings suggest that heart disease remains the leading cause of death in the U.S. , claiming more than  900,000 lives in 2023 alone. Chronic high blood pressure (referred to as hypertension medically) is one of the key early risk factors. Around half of all Americans likely have it, but an estimated four in ten people don’t know they have it, partly because it often does not present with any clear symptoms. And while hypertension is treatable when caught early, many simply don’t see a doctor often enough to be screened regularly. That combination of an invisible condition and spotty screening makes the issue an attractive target for always-on smartwatch sensors.

Sources indicate that the sensors on commercial smartwatches can pick up useful data, but those signals still need to be interpreted by an AI model. In this case, Google says it trained its system on nearly 500,000 hours of sensor data collected from 2,109 people. The optical sensor captures the shapes of each pulse wave at the wrist, while the accelerometer shows signs of the subtle physical vibrations that occur at the wrist when blood is ejected from the heart into the aorta. Both of those signal data are cut into 5-second PPG and ACC waveforms. The AI converts those signal snippets into numerical summaries, which Google refers to as an “embedding.”.

It has been revealed that over time, the AI model was able to pore over those different numerical values and determine which types of pulses are likely associated with hypertension. By analyzing data collected from one wearer to the next, the AI sees numerical patterns that distinguish one person’s signals from another. But simply relying on a measurement from one point in time risks introducing what the researcher calls “environmental noise” that can skew results. To account for all that noise, they aggregated the sensors’ data over multiple days of use to establish a wearer’s persistent state. That data then gets fed into a logistic regression classifier, which comes out with a score corresponding to a person’s likelihood of having hypertension.

It has been revealed that the team tested their system on 196 participants over seven days of real-world monitoring, checking their results against 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, which they refer to as the “gold standard” in the field. The AI smartwatch system ultimately detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8 percent. That means 65.8 percent of people who were proven to have hypertension were accurately identified by their AI system. That’s far from perfect, but it was still higher than the 55.3 percent caught by initial office cuff readings in the study.

“Taken together, the results show that our system can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed BP devices in the existing clinical framework,” Google notes.

Like Apple before it, Google and the other medical researchers involved in this story were quick to stress that these findings, noteworthy as they may sound, shouldn’t lead people to think of this system as a complete replacement for clinical blood pressure monitoring .Going to see actual human doctors isn’t going away anytime soon, but this system, if widely accessible, could help nudge more people towards getting checked out.

The Kids Are Outside: The Rise of the Adult Children’s ADU

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when Diane and Steve Weaver of Castro Valley, California, shipped their son Sam off to college in 2013, they hoped he’d someday find his dream job and a nice home.
  • While in-law suites and granny flats (a nickname for when ADUs house in-laws) have become popular among young, successful homeowners who want their elderly parents nearby, a growing number of Americans are now adding ADUs to their properties to house adult children threatening to move back in and reverse their status as empty nesters.
  • According to recent reports, blame the return of the flock on the home affordability crisis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when Diane and Steve Weaver of Castro Valley, California, shipped their son Sam off to college in 2013, they hoped he’d someday find his dream job and a nice home. And while Sam is thriving professionally as a sales rep with his own place, they never expected that his house would be in their backyard. But the nightmarish Bay Area real estate market made a 400-square-foot ADU (accessory dwelling unit) on his parents’ property, complete with a separate entrance and direct street access, seem like the best option for the 32-year-old. “It was becoming difficult for him to afford rent while also saving toward eventually buying a place of his own,” Diane tells AD. “He’s close by, but it really feels like he has his own home.”.

While in-law suites and granny flats (a nickname for when ADUs house in-laws) have become popular among young, successful homeowners who want their elderly parents nearby, a growing number of Americans are now adding ADUs to their properties to house adult children threatening to move back in and reverse their status as empty nesters.

Diane and Steve Weaver on their property’s ADU.

According to recent reports, blame the return of the flock on the home affordability crisis. These days a homebuyer needs an annual income between $110,000 and $113,000—well above the national average income of $64,220 per year—to comfortably afford a median-priced home in the US, which is currently priced at $434,900. While this has led some grown kids to move back into their childhood bedrooms, in cases where acreage allows, families like the Weavers are opting to be neighbors instead of housemates by setting up self-contained living spaces on the same lot as their single-family homes. In California, they’re certainly no outlier. The state has passed legislation specifically encouraging the construction of ADUs to address the housing shortage—which resulted in quadruple the number of ADU permits issued in the Golden State from 2017 to 2022.

Those in the ADU construction game say families like the Weavers make up an increasingly large slice of their business. Jeremy Nova, co-founder of the Colorado-based prefab ADU builder Studio Home, indicates ADUs for adult children are popular among his clients because the arrangement is mutually beneficial. The kids are afforded some independence and the ability to save money, “while for the parents, it can also be a long-term investment. The same space that houses an adult child today could eventually become a rental or a separate living space for a caregiver.” ADU builders on the opposite coast are seeing the same demand. Justin Olewack, president of Bolt Builders, says that ADUs for adult children are becoming a top request among his clientele in the DC, Virginia, and Maryland areas, where housing costs have risen 61 percent since 2016.

If it cuts costs and results in a sellable amenity down the line, perhaps moving back home isn’t the failure-to-launch scenario it was once seen as.

An ADU by Studio Home, built in the backyard of a Scottsdale, Arizona, family’s property.

It has been revealed that once a family’s adult child moves out of the property’s ADU, especially if it has a kitchen and bathroom, the structure can serve as a rental, providing passive income for retired parents. Tracy Noh, who hired John Brennan of BZBuild Co to build her daughter Eliza Bowen an ADU in Burbank, was thinking long-term with her compound planning. “An in-home apartment would require sharing the space of our 1,000-square-foot main home. And, as someone who works from home, the ADU seemed a better solution,” she says.

Noh and Eliza show off their Burbank ADU.

Industry observers note that the living arrangement has also enabled Noh and her daughter to develop their own life paths. The structure gives her daughter a space in which she can become a young adult, and Noh the opportunity to step back from making the day-to-day household decisions. The former is learning how to manage her own household: planning meals, budgeting expenses, and making time for household chores.

Sources indicate that “That change in dynamic also allows us both to remain much calmer in our interactions with each other,” Noh says. It’s not just because there’s a separate place for each of them to retreat to; Noh says she has “gained an enormous amount of respect for Eliza and her ability to manage her own home. It’s a fabulous opportunity to begin to build that adult-to-adult relationship with your child.”.

The interior of Tracy Noh’s ADU by BZBuild Co.

While modest ADUs serve single occupants just fine, more sizable ADUs allow a family’s adult children to bring their own kids in tow. Oren Amir, co-founder of SoCal builder GO Home Builders, points out that in his experience, the catalyst for aging parents to build an ADU for their adult children is almost never just the adult child themselves: It’s the grandchild they will be bringing with them. “The call comes a few months before or after a baby arrives,” he claims. The grandparents don’t want to travel to visit their grandkids; they want them living nearby. Rent in Los Angeles is what stops people from saving, and early parenthood is when saving matters most, Amir says. An ADU in a grandparent’s backyard, therefore, lets the adult children stay in the neighborhood, raise the baby near help, and set some money aside for when the time comes to leave the nest for good. “Everyone gets what they need and nobody has to move in,” Amir says of the arrangement.

While the Weaver family ADU is Sam’s for now, it could grow up to be a granny flat someday. “It’s possible that Sam might live in the main house and we could move into the ADU as we age,” says Diane. “It gives us a lot of options for how the space can be used as our family’s needs change.”.

On October 27, Healthgrades declared the recipients of the 2027 Specialty Excellence Outpatient Awards and Specialty State Rankings.

Industry observers note that the annual awards recognize hospitals delivering outstanding patient outcomes in specialty care across the United States. Healthgrades is the leading platform used by Americans for finding a doctor or hospital.

New research from Healthgrades highlights that hospital quality is increasingly a factor in healthcare decisions.

Around 80% of patients report that when looking for a doctor, the quality of the hospital where they practice matters. Additionally, 7 in 10 patients (68%) say they’re more likely to seek care for a procedure or health condition from a doctor who works at a hospital with high quality ratings.

What’s more, around 71% of patients say they would switch doctors to gain access to a higher-rated hospital.

“Our specialty awards identify the nation’s top-performing hospitals across numerous medical specialties, helping consumers find high quality care tailored to their specific needs,” stated Alana Biggers, MD, MPH, medical advisor at Healthgrades.

Healthgrades identifies hospitals that deliver exceptional outcomes across common outpatient procedures and specialty conditions.

Finding high quality care is crucial, particularly amid a growing gap between top-performing and one-star hospitals.

“One of the biggest challenges is balancing increasing patient needs with the resources available to healthcare professionals,” Biggers said.

“Hospitals face workforce shortages, growing administrative responsibilities, financial pressures, and increasing complexity in patient care. Physicians and other healthcare professionals need adequate time and support not only to evaluate and treat patients, but also to communicate results, coordinate follow-up care, and address concerns that arise between visits,” she continued.

“When healthcare teams are adequately supported, they are better positioned to communicate effectively with patients, coordinate care, and address patients’ needs.”.

Biggers said that ensuring equal access to quality healthcare is challenging because of factors such as:.

According to recent reports, hospital closures and reduced services make access even more difficult. Biggers identified a few possible solutions, such as expanding outpatient care, building community partnerships, using telehealth when appropriate, and improving coordination among healthcare providers.

“Ultimately, providing high quality care requires more than clinical expertise. It requires healthcare systems to invest in their workforce, strengthen care coordination, and create environments where healthcare professionals have the resources they need to provide safe, effective, and patient-centered care,” Biggers said.

“Equally crucial, healthcare systems must ensure that patients have meaningful access to these services, regardless of where they live or their socioeconomic circumstances.”.

Patients want to find a hospital that excels in the procedures or health conditions relevant to them.

The recipients of the Specialty Excellence Awards are among the top 15% of hospitals specializing in these areas.

“An outstanding hospital prioritizes both patient care and the people delivering that care,” Biggers told Healthline.

This means ensuring physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals have appropriate staffing levels, adequate clinical and administrative support, and opportunities for continued professional development,” she continued.

Healthgrades awards U.S. hospitals that excel at Outpatient Orthopedic Surgery, Outpatient Joint Replacement, andOutpatient Prostate Care.

In a recent development, outpatient care is one of the fastest-growing areas of healthcare. The number of orthopedic procedures performed in an outpatient environment has grown exponentially in recent years.

From 2020 to 2025, outpatient hip replacement procedures grew by 81%, while inpatient procedures dropped by 75%. Outpatient knee replacements increased by 71% while inpatient volumes decreased by 70%.

“I believe several factors are contributing to the growing demand for outpatient care, including advances in medical technology, a greater emphasis on preventive care, and the increasing need to manage chronic medical conditions,” Biggers noted.

In a recent development, “Many services and procedures that previously required hospitalization can now be safely performed in outpatient settings. Patients also appreciate the convenience of receiving care closer to home and avoiding unnecessary hospital stays,” she added.

This is part of the Men's Health Body Bible, a collection of cutting-edge stories focused on helping you build more muscle using the latest science and lessons from some of the finest athletes and trainers on the planet.

THE SECRET TO training your abs is out—and it entails more than situps and planks, more than just targeting your rectus abdominis, the ballyhooed band of muscle between your chest and your hips. If you want true core strength (and, yes, that six-pack), a growing group of experts will tell you that you need to carry heavy weights and walk. This forces your core to constantly microcorrect and rebalance as you move, explains Aaron Horschig, C.S.C.S., D.P.T., a St. Louis–based physical therapist. You also need to twist and turn, challenging your oblique muscles and back extensors.

“While there’s nothing wrong with training the abs for show, training for stability—which encompasses all of the muscles that surround the spine and hips—is essential training for everyone,” notes Horschig. His new book, Rebuilding Milo, includes a variety of exercises, many of which challenge your entire core—think lower back extensors, glutes, and obliques, which all team up with your abs to stabilize and bolster your back, lending postural support.

In a recent development, unlike body parts that handle just one or two tasks (like your biceps, which are most heavily utilized to bend your elbows), all those core muscles have a host of responsibilities. They work together to flex your spine (as happens during a classic situp), and they help rotate your shoulders so you can turn to look at a friend. They also prevent excessive rounding of the lower back (known as anti-flexion), a key tactic in the battle to stop back pain. The ideal abs regimen trains all these functions, protecting you against injuries and readying your core (and spine) for anything life can throw at you. Horschig states people finally get that. “More and more people are starting to understand the true role of core,” he says.

It has been revealed that the end result of all this work? A lower back that’s armor-plated against persistent pain, and the ability to move athletically and fluidly. And along the way, you’ll build those six-pack abs, too.

HOW TO DO IT:An underrated plank upgrade, this move challenges your abs and obliques (and your glutes, too!). Start in pushup position, feet wide. Lift your left hand and touch it to your right shoulder. Keep your hips square as you do. Repeat on the other side.

REPS & SETS:Work for time, not reps, doing three 40-second sets.

According to recent reports, HOW TO DO IT:Stand in a split stance, left shoulder next to the high pulley of a cable machine, both hands grasping the handle, then bend at the knees until your left thigh is nearly parallel to the floor. Keep your hips square to the front as you pull the cable across your body, then return it to the start.

In a recent development, REPS & SETS:Do 10 to 12 reps per side. Do 3 sets.

It has been revealed that HOW TO DO IT:Stand holding kettlebells in both hands, the left bell at your chest, the right bell at your hip. Walk forward (or march in place) for 10 to 15 steps per leg. Move slowly, working to keep your hips square.

REPS & SETS:Do 2 sets per side, challenging your abs and lower-back muscles to keep you upright against the heavy load.

TRAIN YOUR ABS EVERYDAY. Some muscle groups require several days to recover, but your core muscles are built to be resilient. That means you can train them nearly every day. Consider doing 3 or 4 sets of core work in every work- out, rotating in latest and different ab exercises to continually challenge your rectus abdominis, oblique muscles, and lower-back spinal erectors.

NEVER GOING HEAVY. Bodyweight planks and situps are a solid starting point for your ab training. But just like any other muscle, core muscles are meant to be loaded and overloaded. Add resistance to your core training, and don’t be afraid to challenge yourself, especially on moves like the mixed-rack carry above. “You have to do that sometimes,” states the popular bodybuilder and trainer known as Ulisses Jr. “I’d be lying if I told you I didn’t load my abs.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, your typical 2023 BMW M2 has an electronically limited top speed of 155 miles per hour. However, the optional M Driver's Package raises that limit to 177 mph. According to the Arizona Department of Public Safety (AZDPS) Highway Patrol, one M2 driver was apparently determined to explore the upper limits of his car's performance before trading it in; a state trooper clocked him traveling 170 mph on the highway, and criminal charges followed.

The incident happened on November 9, 2026, on Arizona State Route 202 near Sky Harbor Boulevard in Tempe, Arizona. According to authorities, an AZDPS Highway Patrol State Trooper spotted the BMW traveling at a high rate of speed and passing other vehicles. Using a LIDAR device, the trooper reportedly recorded the vehicle traveling 170 mph in a posted 65-mph zone—an astonishing 105 mph over the limit.

Sources indicate that police were not going to engage in a pursuit at that speed, however, and said they decided to use the Highway Patrol Traffic Operations Center to track the vehicle's whereabouts. Eventually the BMW exited the highway, and police were then able to stop the car. At this time, the police reportedly noticed that the BMW didn’t have a license plate.

It has been revealed that police say the officer asked the driver how fast he thought he was going, and the man estimated his speed at approximately 110 to 115 mph. That's still far above the posted speed limit, but nowhere near the 170 mph that had him approaching Daytona 500 qualifying territory. The driver later claimed he hadn't realized just how fast he was traveling, according to authorities.

It has been revealed that why was he driving so fast? He reportedly told the trooper he was planning to trade in the BMW and wanted to take it for one last drive. Hopefully his latest car will be slower than the M2, because as police pointed out in their social media post, at 170 mph, the BMW was traveling approximately 250 feet every second. A crash at that speed would be devastating.

The driver was, unsurprisingly, arrested for reckless driving and endangerment, due to his excessive speed and unsafe driving behavior.

Here are the coolest e-motorcycles and gear we saw at EICMA 2026

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2046 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase.
  • Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.
  • LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet, showing just how far the manufacturer has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase. That means that all of the newest electric motorcycle announcements happen in one place, and we get a chance to check out the coolest developments and most interesting newly introduced gear.

Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.

LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet, showing just how far the manufacturer has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.

In a recent development, the newly introduced S4 Honcho family was a major focus, including the street-oriented Honcho Street, off-road Honcho Trail, and newly unveiled Honcho Skate, a stripped-down addition to the modular platform. The booth also included LiveWire’s larger S2 electric motorcycles, creating a pretty broad spectrum from lightweight urban machines up through full-size highway-capable electric motorcycles.

The other massive piece of the booth was DUST Moto, which LiveWire acquired earlier this year. The production-intent DUST Hightail was displayed alongside the newly revealed DUST Spur, giving LiveWire an immediate presence in the increasingly popular lightweight electric dirt bike category.

Add in STACYC’s electric balance bikes for young riders, and the entire booth almost looked like an electric two-wheeler progression chart: start a kid on a STACYC, move up through lightweight DUST and Honcho machines, and eventually graduate to a full-size LiveWire.

GR1T Motorcycles is a relatively young European electric motorcycle startup that caught my eye at EICMA with its G1 platform, a lightweight electric motorcycle designed and engineered in Italy. The basic recipe is pretty compelling: 130 km/h (81 mph) top speed, 11 kW of continuous power and 26.6 kW (36 hp) peak, all while weighing just 130 kg (287 lb).

Industry observers note that perhaps most importantly for urban riders, its roughly 6 kWh battery is actually split into two removable 3 kWh packs, meaning apartment dwellers can pull the batteries out and charge them inside. They’re big, but removing them is doable.

GR1T’s bikes therefore pack in around 50% more battery capacity than most electric motorcycles in this size and weight class, meaning roughly 50% more range, as well.

There are also some interesting and clever design choices, like the underslung rear suspension and the triple-camera system that includes front and rear dashcams plus a cockpit-facing camera for recording the rider.

According to recent reports, the clever part of the overall design scheme is that GR1T isn’t developing a separate platform for every motorcycle. The same basic G1 chassis, motor, batteries, belt drive, and electronics underpin four versions: the G1S Street, G1X Scrambler, G1XR Raider, and utility-oriented G1M Mission.

Prices are set to start at €8,495 including VAT, putting these squarely in that emerging category of reasonably affordable, lightweight electric motorcycles that have enough speed for real-world commuting without chasing superbike performance.

Industry observers note that there’s an notable caveat, though: these aren’t production motorcycles yet. GR1T states it is presently fundraising, with factory development and pre-orders set to follow after funding closes and first deliveries now targeted for the first half of 2028.

So the bikes aren’t quite ready for primetime yet, but it’s definitely a firm to watch.

Real Motors brought one of the more visually striking electric motorcycles to EICMA with Project: ARES, a futuristic electric café racer that the American startup describes as an “Electric Analog” machine – basically an attempt to preserve the raw, mechanical connection of motorcycling while ditching unnecessary screens and gadgetry.

And there’s plenty of performance underneath the sci-fi bodywork: Real Motors lists a 75 kW (100 hp) motor, a 15 kWh battery, a 120 mph (192 km/h) top speed, and an estimated weight of 485 lb (220 kg).

The analog analogy is spot on, with the display probably the simplest and most straightforward I’ve ever seen on an electric motorcycle. There’s also no app, no subscription, and no digital handcuffs. The bike is very much the electric equivalent of a simple ICE bike that just rides, albeit with a much nicer ride.

Unlike many of the futuristic concepts scattered around EICMA, ARES is actually headed toward limited production.

Real Motors plans to build just 250 examples in its first LOT 01 production run, with pricing starting at $20,000 and North American deliveries targeted for early 2027. European deliveries are expected after homologation is completed.

The manufacturer has also brought former LiveWire CTO Vance Strader onto the project as it makes the difficult transition from a very cool prototype into an actual production motorcycle.

I actually had the chance to do a spin on the bike, and so I’ll be reporting back on the experience. But you can tell from my smile below that the ride was quite an experience!

Seatylock has been my go-to e-bike lock company for several years now, and I use their locks for my several e-bikes and my wife’s e-bike too.

Now Seatylock has returned with some even more impressive locks. The firm demonstrated off its fresh Ultra D28 lock, which is both angle grinder-proof and wide enough to lock the wheel of a motorcycle. It solves the problem of how do you make a lock strong enough for a motorcycle but also small and light enough that you can actually carry it with you, unlike a massive chain lock that usually stays where you park your motorcycle overnight.

In the image below, you can see the shackle next to an exposed section demonstrating the diamond coating that essentially destroys angle grinder discs – even diamond coated discs.

The manufacturer also has a slightly smaller version of the same lock designed for bicycles.

Both will absolutely destroy even the toughest angle grinder discs. Sure, eventually someone could cut through them, but it may take a dozen discs and by that point the thief has moved on to an easier target.

At EICMA 2026, Royal Enfield continued expanding its electric motorcycle ambitions with its Flying Flea sub-brand, showcasing the scrambler-style motorcycle alongside its growing lineup of lightweight, retro-inspired electric motorcycles.

There were several interesting colorways and customized designs on display, showcasing the Flying Flea’s stylish design.

The new models blend Royal Enfield’s classic design heritage with modern electric technology, targeting urban riders and those looking for a fun, approachable electric motorcycle rather than a high-performance machine.

With distinctive styling, compact proportions, and an emphasis on accessible riding, the Flying Flea lineup represents Royal Enfield’s effort to carve out a place in the emerging market for smaller electric motorcycles while maintaining the character that has made its gasoline-powered bikes so popular.

Yamaha showed off its new NMAX E electric scooter, bringing battery-powered performance to one of the brand’s most recognizable urban scooter families.

Designed as an electric alternative to the popular gasoline-powered NMAX, the newly introduced model combines familiar sporty styling with a quiet, low-maintenance electric drivetrain aimed at everyday city commuting.

The NMAX E uses Yamaha’s fresh compact eAxle powertrain, shared with the larger-wheeled XENTER E, and delivers up to 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power, putting it in the 125cc-equivalent class.

With its practical step-through design, automatic operation, and approachable performance, the NMAX E represents another step in Yamaha’s push to electrify its urban mobility lineup, particularly in European markets where scooters are already a popular alternative to cars.

Segway indicated off a new vision for safer electric scooters, including its futuristic X Cruiser concept that takes rider protection to a whole new level.

Rather than relying solely on traditional motorcycle safety equipment, the X Cruiser explores automotive-inspired features such as integrated seats with seatbelts, partial enclosures, and even a fully roofed version designed to offer additional protection from the elements.

In a recent development, the concept includes several configurations, ranging from a more conventional open scooter to a partially enclosed design and a fully covered model that looks like a cross between a motorcycle and a tiny electric car. While these designs are still concepts rather than production-ready scooters, they demonstrate how Segway is rethinking two-wheeled transportation by exploring ways to make electric scooters safer, more comfortable, and potentially more appealing to riders who might otherwise be hesitant to trade four wheels for two.

Eli Electric Vehicles took to EICMA 2026 to display its compact Eli Zero electric quadricycle, a tiny two-seat urban EV designed to offer much of the convenience of a car without the size, weight, or expense of a conventional automobile.

With its enclosed cabin, side-by-side seating, and ultra-compact footprint, the Eli Zero offers a practical alternative to larger vehicles for short city trips, combining the weather protection and comfort of a car with the maneuverability and efficiency of a much smaller vehicle.

Recent findings suggest that the firm revealed a more powerful L7e-class version of the Eli Zero that it had previously teased, expanding the vehicle’s capabilities beyond its existing L6e configuration. The upcoming Race Edition also pushes the envelope farther with custom interior and a few extra accents to the body.

With growing interest in smaller, more efficient urban transportation, Eli’s presence at EICMA definitely underlined how the show is increasingly embracing electric mobility solutions that go beyond traditional motorcycles and scooters.

NIU revealed off its latest lineup of electric scooters, continuing the brand’s push to make battery-powered two-wheelers a practical alternative to gasoline-powered urban transportation. Known for its sleek designs, connected technology, and approachable electric scooters, NIU highlighted models aimed at a range of riders, from everyday city commuters to those looking for more powerful machines capable of keeping up with faster urban traffic.

The organization showed off several upcoming models for the 2027 model year, with scooters that combine modern styling with features such as smartphone connectivity, smart security systems, and efficient electric drivetrains, all while maintaining the simplicity and low operating costs that make electric scooters so appealing.

While I didn’t see anything groundbreaking at the brand’s booth this year, the incremental updates look to push newly introduced tech features further throughout the brand’s many models, helping more of NIU’s offerings enter that premium level that the organization has been known for.

For something a bit wilder, Honda shared its futuristic EV Outlier Concept, an electric motorcycle that explores what two-wheeled design could look like when engineers are freed from the constraints of traditional gasoline-powered motorcycles.

Industry observers note that with its long, low-slung profile, radically different riding position, and futuristic bodywork, the EV Outlier looks more like something out of a science fiction movie than a conventional motorcycle. The concept features electric motors integrated into both wheels, giving it two-wheel drive while opening up upcoming possibilities for packaging and weight distribution.

Rather than simply replacing a combustion engine with a battery and motor, Honda used the EV Outlier to rethink the entire motorcycle layout, demonstrating how electrification could lead to entirely fresh types of riding experiences.

While the bike remains a design concept with no revealed production looks, it offers an intriguing glimpse into Honda’s vision for the future of electric motorcycles.

Recent findings suggest that vespa showed off its next-generation electric scooter lineup at EICMA, including electric versions of the Primavera, Sprint S, and Primavera Tech. While they don’t look radically different, there’s a lot more happening underneath the familiar steel bodywork.

A new Italian-made, rare-earth-free electric motor improves efficiency and performance, while the 45 km/h Primavera and Sprint S now feature removable batteries.

The faster 67 km/h Primavera Tech gets up to 90 km of WMTC range – a 12.5% improvement – along with an updated vehicle management system and more efficient charger.

AHEAD OF THE fall, I knew I was going to need a sickening boot that could just fall in line with my entire wardrobe. I don’t spend much on clothes, because, well, I wear-test them for a living, but when it comes to shopping for footwear I’ve been guilty of dropping more bread than I’d like to admit. There are times I don’t mind dishing out a little cash for a well-made shoe, especially if that means I’ll have it for years to come. One style that was calling my name that I couldn’t resist was Our Legacy’s Camion Boot.

Recent findings suggest that if you’ve spent any time scrolling through men’s fashion content on Instagram or TikTok, chances are you’ve come across it. Even actor Paul Mescal has been spotted wearing the boot during a press tour for “Hamnet” in London. The sleek leather ankle-high boot has become something of a cult favorite among stylish guys, thanks to its distinctive square toe and minimalist design, which helps make any simple outfit look 10 times cooler. Whether I’m wearing baggy jeans or relaxed trousers, The Camion Boot adds a certain je ne sais quoi that my cowboy or lace-up boots can’t replicate. And by no means does the boot feel squishy like your favorite pair of sneakers, but the Vibram rubber outsole keeps my feet comfortable on days when I'm standing and walking around for hours.

For those unfamiliar, Our Legacy is a Swedish fashion label founded in Stockholm in 2005. Over the past two decades, the brand has built a loyal following for taking menswear staples and remixing them with unique proportions, fabrics, and details. The Camion Boot is one of its most recognizable designs, decorated with an inside zip closure and a metal branded tab. It feels timeless without looking boring. Even though it’s easy on the eyes, its $700-plus price tag is tough on the wallet. Luckily, you don’t have to cough up designer money to get the look. Below, I’ve gathered a list of affordable alternatives that deliver the same vibe for a fraction of the price.

If you’re looking for a boot that captures the sleek appeal of Our Legacy’s Camion without spending a small fortune, Florsheim’s Medford is a strong contender. The leather upper has a subtle burnished finish that delivers a slightly worn-in look, as the clean silhouette makes it easy to dress up or down. I’d pair the brown version with black denim and a chunky sweater for dinner followed by a night out. It also looks sharp with dressy pants and tailored trousers, so you can get plenty of mileage out of it at the office.

It has been revealed that inside, there’s a fully cushioned, removable footbed made with OrthoLite rebound foam, which helps absorb impact and provides a little extra bounce underfoot. This comes in handy if you’re spending hours on your feet. The leather is also designed to feel comfortable from the jump, so you shouldn’t have to suffer through a lengthy break-in period. And while I wouldn’t treat these like rain boots, the leather construction makes them a practical choice for everyday wear, especially with proper care. You don’t have to settle for a black colorway either—it comes in a few different brown shades as well.

Industry observers note that zara offers a squared-off toe that is unapologetically bold, giving the boot that exaggerated, fashion-forward shape that makes Our Legacy’s Camion so recognizable. I’d argue the toe is even more pronounced here, which isn’t necessarily a bad thing if you want your footwear to stand out more. I’d style these with relaxed jeans that fall just over the shaft or wide-leg trousers to really lean into the silhouette.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest difference comes down to the material. Unlike the Camion, Zara’s version is made from polyurethane, a synthetic material that mimics the appearance of leather, so it’s a budget-friendly pick. It’s generally easy to wipe clean, but it won’t develop the same natural patina as genuine leather and can eventually peel or crack with repeated wear.

Industry observers note that steve Madden’s Ronco might be the closest style to the Camion boot as far as design is concerned. It nailed the features from the stitched detailing across the upper right down to the substantial rubber sole. The latter is worth pointing out because it gives the boot a similar sturdy, grounded appearance, while the 1.5-inch heel adds just enough height without going overboard. Sure, the rounded toe isn’t quite as boxy as the Camion’s signature square shape, but the overall silhouette comes pretty darn close. And at a fraction of the price, it’s hard not to appreciate the resemblance.

According to recent reports, I’m especially drawn to the brown leather version, which has a rich, burnished finish that shifts between lighter and darker shades, giving it a slightly weathered, vintage effect. It has a lot more depth than your standard brown boot. I’d pair these with relaxed denim and a chunky sweater for an easy apple-picking look, or throw them on with tailored trousers and a leather jacket for something a little sharper. There’s also a black option if you prefer to keep things simple.

Banana Republic takes a different approach with this Italian leather Chelsea-style boot. The silhouette is sleek and understated, but what really caught my attention is the leather’s distressed finish. It has that subtly weathered, almost cracked appearance you’d normally expect from a well-loved pair of boots, except the detail is already built into the design. It gives the shoe a vintage feel without looking like something that’s been sitting in the back of your closet for a decade. I also appreciate that this pair doesn’t try too hard to replicate the Camion. Instead, it offers a more classic interpretation that feels right at home with the rest of my wardrobe. I’d wear it with pleated trousers and a button-down for the office, then swap in straight-leg jeans and a crewneck for a day of shopping.

Sources indicate that camper has a knack for taking classic footwear and giving it a slightly unexpected twist, which perfectly describes the Dean Boot. The black-and-burgundy color combination immediately caught my attention because it’s subtle enough to wear with anything, but there’s also a richness to the pebbled leather texture that makes it more interesting than your standard black ankle boot. I’d pair these with relaxed black trousers or dark denim and let the boots bring a little personality to the outfit.

The upper combines calfskin leather with recycled PET, which is plastic recycled from materials like water bottles, and latex for added flexibility. Underfoot, there’s a removable OrthoLite footbed for cushioning and an XL Extralight EVA outsole, a lightweight foam-based material designed to absorb impact without weighing you down. I also appreciate the pull tab, which makes slipping them on a little easier, especially since there’s no traditional side zipper. Plus, the defined heel and outsole design offer some stability for walking, though actual traction will depend on the surface.

I’ve owned my Frye boots for about a year now, and they’ve more than earned their place in my footwear rotation. They’re so versatile, I can wear them with a suit one day and jeans, a T-shirt, and leather jacket the next. The design is minimal with a premium leather upper and stitching around the edge that adds to the sturdy construction. Comfort-wise, I didn’t have to deal with that annoying break-in period that often comes with leather boots.

After a year of wear, the leather has started developing some natural creases, but I look at it like it adds character. There’s enough wiggle room in the toe box that my feet don’t feel cramped. The inner side zipper is another detail I’ve come to appreciate, especially when I’m taking them off after a long day. I’ve put these through their paces on city streets and even worn them in the rain. I found the leather has dried quickly after getting wet, and the grip has felt secure underfoot. Sure, they’re not cheap, but considering how well they’ve held up and how often I wear them, I’d say I’ve already gotten my money’s worth.

According to recent reports, if you’re a guy who gets suited up more often than not, Suitsupply’s leather boot deserves a spot on your radar. It’s the dressiest option on this list, with a smooth, semi-matte leather, which catches just enough light to look sharp without being overly shiny. It also has a fine, tight grain, which gives the surface a supple finish. I’d wear these with a charcoal suit or tailored black trousers and a crisp button-down, for a holiday party. But I would also style them with dark denim and a cashmere sweater. The side zipper makes getting dressed a little less of a production in the morning. The leather sole adds to that dress-shoe appeal, although I’d be a little more cautious wearing these on slick pavement.

In a recent development, now, these are the most expensive boots on this list, but because they’re made in Italy using Blake-stitched construction, a technique that stitches the upper directly to the sole for a slimmer, more flexible profile than you’d typically get with bulkier boot construction. You can expect some natural creasing after a few wears, particularly where your foot bends, but that doesn’t mean the leather is cracking.

To keep it from drying out, Suitsupply recommends applying shoe polish at least once a month, or more frequently if you’re wearing them daily. This helps maintain the color and adds some protection against moisture. I’d also work in a leather conditioner whenever the material starts feeling dry to help prevent actual cracking. It’s a little extra maintenance, sure, but worthwhile if you’re investing this much in a pair of boots.

#29595. Muscle Size vs. Strength: Which Matters More for Living Longer? Experts Explain

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1750 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

Muscle Size vs. Strength: Which Matters More for Living Longer? Experts Explain

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When it comes to aging well, you've probably heard that building muscle is one of the best things you can do for your body.
  • Resistance training, which is often used as an umbrella term, can have different goals, including building muscle size and increasing maximal strength.
  • Industry observers note that on the other hand, training for maximal strength focuses on improving how much force your muscles can produce.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to aging well, you've probably heard that building muscle is one of the best things you can do for your body. And it's true: Maintaining muscle mass is essential for staying healthy, mobile, and independent as you get older. But here's something you might not realize: Having more muscle doesn't necessarily mean you're stronger. And when it comes to living as long (and as well!) as possible, that distinction matters.

Resistance training, which is often used as an umbrella term, can have different goals, including building muscle size and increasing maximal strength. Training for muscle growth, known as hypertrophy training, focuses on increasing the size of your muscles, indicates Vonda Wright, MD, an orthopedic surgeon who researches longevity and muscle health.

Industry observers note that on the other hand, training for maximal strength focuses on improving how much force your muscles can produce. It’s often measured by how much weight you can lift in a particular exercise, Dr. Wright explains. Although larger muscles have the potential to produce more force, muscle size alone doesn’t determine strength. “That’s why someone who is smaller can sometimes be stronger than someone with visibly larger muscles,” she adds.

Meet the experts: Vonda Wright, MD, is an orthopedic surgeon and author of Unbreakable. Mark Kovacs, PhD, CSCS, is an exercise physiologist, longevity and human performance specialist, and founder of the Kovacs Institute in Atlanta. Stuart Phillips, PhD, is a muscle researcher and professor of kinesiology at McMaster University. Ben Walker, CPT, is a personal trainer and founder of Anywhere Fitness in Dublin, Ireland.

Industry observers note that still, both adaptations play an important role in healthy aging—especially since muscle mass and strength naturally decline with age. Building muscle supports your joints and bones, helps regulate metabolic health, and gives you the strength and physical capacity to keep moving and stay active, claims Mark Kovacs, PhD, CSCS, an exercise physiologist, longevity and human performance specialist, and founder of the Kovacs Institute. Strength, meanwhile, allows you to put that muscle to work, whether you’re carrying groceries, climbing stairs, or getting up from the floor, he explains.

It’s imperative to build both strength and muscle for a long, healthy life. But if your goal is to stay active and independent well into your later years, one may be worth prioritizing over the other.

Sources indicate that resistance training can help you build muscle and become stronger, but these are distinct goals that emphasize different outcomes. Training for muscle growth focuses on increasing muscle size, while training for maximal strength focuses on improving how much force you can produce, says Kovacs. The two goals overlap, and people typically gain both muscle and strength through resistance training. But you can formulate your workouts to emphasize one outcome over the other, he adds.

According to recent reports, for instance, if your goal is maximal strength, the weight you lift matters more. So, training for strength means practicing movements with loads that feel heavy to you, indicates Stuart Phillips, PhD, a muscle researcher and professor of kinesiology at McMaster University. Strength gains depend not only on muscle size, but also on how effectively your nervous system activates your muscles and how efficiently you perform the movement. “Lighter weights can still make you stronger, but taking them to failure doesn’t automatically make them equivalent to heavier training for maximizing strength,” Phillips explains. For this goal, he recommends 2 to 3 sets of roughly 4 to 8 reps with a challenging weight, stopping before your technique breaks down.

In terms of muscle growth, both lighter and heavier weights can build muscle—what matters is that your body is sufficiently challenged. Of course, lighter weights will require more repetitions to grow muscle, Phillips claims. (In fact, his research reveals that performing roughly 20 to 25 repetitions with light weights produced similar muscle growth to sets of 8 to 12 repetitions with heavier weights when both were taken to failure.).

According to recent reports, as a rule of thumb, Phillips recommends choosing a weight that makes the last few reps feel challenging while leaving about two good reps in reserve. (If you finish 25 reps and feel like you could easily do five more, the weight is probably too light to provide enough of a stimulus to spark growth.) One way to gauge this is with the resistance-training rating of perceived exertion (RPE) scale, which measures how hard a set feels based on how many more reps you think you could complete with good form, he explains. The scale runs from 1 to 10: An RPE of eight means you could squeeze out about two more reps, a 9 means you have one left, and a 10 means you’ve reached failure and can’t complete another rep.

According to recent reports, the number of sets you perform matters for building muscle, too. Doing one challenging set per exercise consistently over time can grow muscle, Phillips notes, but research suggests that performing multiple sets generally leads to greater muscle growth.

Industry observers note that strength, which is the maximum force you can produce in a particular task, directly influences how well you can move through everyday life. “Strong muscles support our skeleton, protect our joints, improve metabolic health, and allow us to continue doing the things we love at 50, 70, and 90,” indicates Dr. Wright. Strength helps us with getting up off the floor, carrying our own suitcase, climbing a mountain, playing with grandchildren, and living independently long-term.

Consider something as simple as getting out of a chair. When you’re younger and stronger, Kovacs states that movement may require only a small percentage of your maximum strength. As you lose strength with age, though, that same movement requires more of what you have available. If you aren’t regularly training it, everyday activities can become increasingly difficult, he explains. But when you continue to build strength as you age, you have more to pull from, making those activities easier.

Sources indicate that additionally, research draws a direct connection between strength and a longer life: A 2026 study in JAMA Network Open looked at the association between muscular strength and mortality. Over 5,000 women ages 63 to 99 underwent testing for grip strength, chair stand performance, and a timed walk test. Participants also mailed health update questionnaires annually between 2012 and 2014 until 2023. They found that higher muscle strength was associated with lower mortality.

Recent findings suggest that strength training is also associated with cardiometabolic benefits, endurance performance, and bone density—which are all crucial for living long and well. In fact, a small 2022 study in Sensors had 29 postmenopausal women with osteopenia or osteoporosis (when you have lower bone mineral density than normal) either do strength training exercises with heavy and moderately heavy weights, or no exercise at all, for six months. The group that strength trained had higher bone mineral density at the end of the trial period.

Muscle is one of your body’s best forms of insurance for getting older. Everyday activities depend on having enough muscle (as well as strength) to do them independently. “Muscle supports our joints and loads our bones, helping stimulate the bone-building process, but it’s also essential to mobility and functional strength," Dr. Wright explains. “If we want to continue getting ourselves off the ground, climbing stairs, carrying things, traveling, playing sports, and living independently, we need muscle to do it.”.

Industry observers note that research also concludes that less muscle mass is associated with a higher risk of mortality. A 2023 review in PLOS One observed 16 studies with over 81,000 participants and looked at the connection between their body composition and when they died. The review concluded that a low skeletal muscle mass index was significantly associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality.

Additionally, having muscle mass can improve your metabolic health. A 2025 study in Nutrition & Metabolism had older participants with type 2 diabetes either build muscle through resistance training alone, resistance training and eating a whey protein supplement, or doing neither of the two, for 12 weeks. Those who completed the muscle-building interventions significantly improved their blood glucose control and insulin resistance.

Sources indicate that plus, lower muscle mass is linked to poor balance and a higher risk of falls. So, maintaining muscle helps protect your mobility and independence as you age, Dr. Wright adds. A 2020 study in Menopause Review had 122 women over 60 do physical performance tests (gait speed test, grip strength, and a timed up and go). Their body composition was measured, and they filled out a survey of how often they fell in the past year. Less muscle was associated with a higher risk of falls.

Sources indicate that A well-rounded workout initiative should naturally progress both muscular size and strength. After all, they address different pieces of the same puzzle and one form of training can help you make progress in the other. As you build muscle, you generally increase the amount of tissue available to produce force, states Ben Walker, CPT, a certified personal trainer and founder of Anywhere Fitness in Dublin, Ireland. And as you train for strength, your brain and nervous system become better at coordinating and activating those muscles, he explains.

In a recent development, if you’re looking for a plan that’ll help you build both strength and muscle, check out our Women’s Health+ exclusive workout plans. Each one comes with four weeks of expert-programmed workouts, science-backed nutrition advice, and evidence-based recovery methods.

Remember, longevity isn’t about simply adding years to your life. It’s about extending your healthspan, or the number of years you remain healthy, mobile, and strong. “The goal is to bring our healthspan as close to our lifespan as possible, and for me, that means building a body that can carry you through the life you want to live,” says Dr. Wright. That way, you’ll be ready to throw grandkids around at 60, deadlift hundreds of pounds at 70, and lift your own suitcase on vacation with your family in your 80s and beyond.

Many of the Muppets are pretty easy to pin down, species-wise. Kermit is a frog. Fozzie is a bear. Miss Piggy is, obviously, a feisty piggy. But Gonzo—with his blue-ish fur, bulging eyes, tuft of purple feathers, and long, curved nose that looks a little like a beak—is something of an enigma. The writers of the Muppets have avoided the question of what Gonzo is for years.

Well, in a new episode of Popular Science’s Ask Us Anything podcast, we asked three biologists to break down exactly what Gonzo is. We also talk to Muppets legend and Gonzo performer Dave Goelz to get his take.

Recent findings suggest that ask Us Anything answers your most outlandish, mind-burning questions—from the everyday things you’ve always wondered to the bizarre things you never thought to ask. So, yes, there’s a reason candy tastes different now and no, you don’t need to worry about Yellowstone’s supervolcano blowing up anytime soon. If you have a question for us, send us a note. Nothing is too silly or simple.

This episode is based on the Popular Science article “What kind of animal is Gonzo?”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Honda’s automatic engine start-stop feature is under latest federal scrutiny, after the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration received hundreds of complaints that engines failed to restart automatically from a complete stop at a traffic light on certain models, prompting the agency to commence an investigation.

According to recent reports, the federal probe, confirmed on Friday, November 13, includes 1.03 million units of the 2024-2026 Honda Passport, Odyssey, Pilot, and Ridgeline. The inquiry also includes 2024-2026 Acura MDX units. NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation received 701 complaints related to the Auto Start/Stop feature.

Industry observers note that “To help improve fuel efficiency, the Auto Start/Stop system will automatically shut off the engine when a vehicle comes to a complete stop. The engine is intended to automatically restart when a driver releases the brake pedal. However, the complaints allege that the engines are failing to restart once they have been shut off by this system,” the investigation announcement reads.

While automatic start-stop systems were created to improve fuel economy, Honda seems to be having a recurring issue with the feature. Federal safety regulators previously opened a probe into Honda’s automatic start-stop system in 2025. That investigation included 2.2 million late-model Honda Pilot, Odyssey, Passport, and Ridgeline models, as well as Acura MDX and TLX units. However, the upcoming investigation includes 2026 model-year units. Inquiry documents allege that the two issue populations have different root causes and respond differently to repairs.

There have been no injuries related to this issue, according to the feds. EPA boss Lee Zeldin noted the agency was investigating improvements or eliminating the technology last year; whether it sticks around in the long run, however, an engineering analysis of the stop-start system should bring Honda and NHTSA together to identify an effective solution to this recurring problem soon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In June, Fresh Mexico State University graduate student William Grooms was using motion-sensing cameras to investigate wildlife in Carson National Forest in northern New Mexico.
  • His cameras had captured a series of photographs of a Canada lynx (Lynx canadensis)—a wild cat that hasn’t been documented in the state for around 25 years.
  • Industry observers note that “It caught my eye because the cat in the image had the characteristic ear tufts and facial ruff [of bobcats], but it was lacking the black spots that are typical of bobcats,” Grooms, who is studying in the department of Fish, Wildlife and Conservation Ecology, tells Popular Science.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In June, Fresh Mexico State University graduate student William Grooms was using motion-sensing cameras to investigate wildlife in Carson National Forest in northern New Mexico. And when he looked through his first images, he spotted something flabbergasting.

His cameras had captured a series of photographs of a Canada lynx (Lynx canadensis)—a wild cat that hasn’t been documented in the state for around 25 years. But Grooms had to make sure it wasn’t actually a bobcat (Lynx rufus), which is a similar-looking species.

Industry observers note that “It caught my eye because the cat in the image had the characteristic ear tufts and facial ruff [of bobcats], but it was lacking the black spots that are typical of bobcats,” Grooms, who is studying in the department of Fish, Wildlife and Conservation Ecology, tells Popular Science. “We also have a good image of the tail, which on lynx has a solid black tip compared to a bobcat whose tail has white on the underside, so my confidence grew.”.

He and his team also demonstrated the image to other researchers for confirmation. Ultimately, there’s no doubt about the fact that the big cat slinking through the dark was indeed a Canada lynx. The species lives in dense boreal and subalpine forests and woodlands throughout much of Canada and Alaska. They have long legs, grayish or yellowish-brown coats, and wide fur-lined paws.

Their main prey are snowshoe hares (Lepus americanus), which they follow into the forest understory—the ground-level area of downed trees and dense vegetation beneath which the hares hide and live. The problem is that these kinds of habitats are fire hazards. Recent forest fire mitigation efforts include decreasing dangerous fuel loads via thinning, prescribed burning, or timber harvesting.

“While these tactics reduce the risk of severe fires, they also remove key habitat features,” Grooms explains. “Our objective is to provide managers with practical, science-based advice regarding what effects fuel reduction treatments and timber harvesting have on wildlife in the Southern Rocky Mountains so that they can make well-informed decisions as they go about their task of managing our nation’s forests.”.

Simply knowing that at least one Canada lynx was in the area provides more data for this mission.

‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’: Inside the Psychedelic 1970s-Inspired Dystopian Sets

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, francis Lawrence, director of The Hunger Games, has a tradition with author Suzanne Collins.
  • Lawrence’s latest adaptation, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (in theaters today), returns to Panem, a postapocalyptic nation where the ruling Capitol controls twelve districts through extreme systemic oppression—most notoriously the titular spectacle in which children are selected by lottery and forced to fight to the death in an arena.
  • District 12’s female tribute Maysilee Donner (McKenna Grace) at the reaping.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, francis Lawrence, director of The Hunger Games, has a tradition with author Suzanne Collins. Before bringing a latest installment of her bestselling dystopian saga to the big screen, the two join forces to envision how the fictional world of Panem will take shape. “I go to New York each time, and we sit in a conference room at Scholastic,” says Lawrence, who has directed five of the franchise’s six films. “We go through the book page by page and beat out what we think the movie is going to look like.”.

Lawrence’s latest adaptation, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (in theaters today), returns to Panem, a postapocalyptic nation where the ruling Capitol controls twelve districts through extreme systemic oppression—most notoriously the titular spectacle in which children are selected by lottery and forced to fight to the death in an arena. Set twenty-four years before the original The Hunger Games (2012) plotline, the prequel follows District 12’s sixteen-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada)—the future mentor (played by Woody Harrelson) to Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson)—as he is selected to fight in the Second Quarter Quell, a particularly sadistic rendition of the Games held every twenty-five years.

District 12’s female tribute Maysilee Donner (McKenna Grace) at the reaping.

Though the dystopia is set in a future North America, the previous prequel, The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes (2023), drew from the architecture of 1940s and ’50s postwar Berlin to depict evil President Snow’s rise to tyranny. Set forty years later, Sunrise explores Panem at a new stage of its evolution. Designed by returning production designer Uli Hanisch, the film follows Haymitch from his impoverished mining district, which barely evolves throughout the series’s sixty-five year timeline, to the opulent Capitol, whose extravagance is expressed through a 1970s-inflected visual lexicon.

“I realized the ’70s fall right smack in the middle between that movie and the originals, so we could lean into that,” claims Lawrence. Hanisch and his team incorporated references to Andy Warhol, Studio 54, and the decade’s psychedelic color palette, appropriating its progressive spirit to convey the Capitol’s opulence and authoritarianism—and, particularly in the arena, using the aesthetic as a means of deception. “To turn the ’70s style from something progressive, liberal, young, and open-minded into something evil is a twist,” says Hanisch. “But that is the key to the entire film’s design.”.

It has been revealed that haymitch and Maysilee as allies in the arena. The forest portion was filmed separately near Cologne, Germany.

The stylistic choice is also a poignant nod to Collins’s original inspiration for the book series. The 1970s marked a transformation in American television: as color TVs became ubiquitous in households across the country, sporting spectacles, variety indicates, and beauty pageants flourished, establishing cultural touchstones that would help shape the contemporary reality programming Collins critiques and satirizes in The Hunger Games. “I was flipping through the channels one night between reality television programs and actual footage of the Iraq War, when the idea came to me,” Collins recalled in a 2018 interview with The Newly introduced York Times. The juxtaposition inspired her to explore just-war theory for young people through an authoritarian dystopia in which mass entertainment is an instrument of political control.

From an abandoned rural steel mill to authoritarian monuments from postwar Berlin, the film draws on politically charged German sites to capture Panem at a pivotal stage in its political and architectural evolution.

In a recent development, production Designer Uli Hanisch at the District 12 set. “District 12 is the most sentimental set to me because I’d known this site near my hometown my entire life,” Hanisch claims.

According to recent reports, to recreate the Appalachian-inspired, deteriorating industrial landscape of District 12 that was shot in Atlanta in the original series, the production utilized a sprawling abandoned steel mill in Duisburg, Germany, Hanisch’s hometown. “I wish we had it in the original movies, because it is an unbelievable space,” Lawrence claims of the post-industrial, rural landscape, which also appeared in The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, Hanisch’s first film in the franchise. “Everywhere you look is exactly how I have always imagined District 12.”.

While District 12 was filmed near Atlanta in the original films, director Francis Lawrence’s fascination with German architecture brought production to Berlin for The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes. It was there that he began collaborating with Berlin-based production designer Hanisch, who proposed this steel mill nearby his hometown for the upcoming location. Upon seeing photographs, Lawrence exclaimed, “Are you kidding me? ... Let’s go tomorrow,” and promptly flew out to see it for himself.

The production designer added modest huts at the edge of a nearby quarry to recreate the Seam, home to Haymitch, his girlfriend Lenore Dove (Whitney Peak), and fellow tribute Louella McCoy (Molly McCann), its humble dwellings contrasting the more prosperous merchant district inhabited by fellow tribute Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace).

It has been revealed that “Unlike the Capitol, District 12 doesn't evolve stylistically throughout the films. Nobody is investing in it, and everything is gradually deteriorating,” Hanisch explains. The vivid purples and oranges of the Capitol’s ‘70s palette are notably absent, only appearing prominently in propaganda decorating the reaping square, including Hunger Games campaign materials and posters portraying Snow as Panem’s number-one Peacekeeper.

Druscilla in the Capitol before the tribute interviews, which is broadcast to all of Panem.

In a recent development, in the Capitol, however, the architecture takes on a distinctly ‘70s flair. Rooted in the Roman concept of panem et circenses, or “bread and circuses,” from which Panem takes its name, the architecture reinforces the government’s manipulation through spectacle. In the background is Berlin's International Congress Centrum, a colossal, aluminum-clad convention center that opened in 1979, which Lawrence describes as “Cold War-era Berlin showing off in a modern way.” As West Berlin’s most expensive postwar building, the futuristic complex was publicly subsidised to showcase economic prosperity and technological advancement—an evocative backdrop for the Capitol’s own display of authoritarianism.

In a recent development, “It’s a time of peace for the Capitol with no rebel attacks, so Snow's had time to build the city up in a way that is an extravagant show of power,” Lawrence explains. The chariot parade, which introduces the tributes before the Games, similarly unfolds against the historically-charged Berlin Olympiastadion, which was designed by Werner March for the 1936 Olympics under Nazi Germany to project state power and an illusion of timeless permanence.

The upstairs library in Plutarch’s home, which he inherited from the Heavensbee dynasty. Reflecting the Capitol’s classic style, it contrasts the Plutarch’s modern downstairs salon which features Warhol-inspired portraits, including one of director Lawrence.

The Capitol's grandeur is also exhibited inside the mansion of Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons), a cameraman with historic ties to Panem’s ruling class. “This was one of my favorite sets because of the scope and scale” Lawrence says, noting how its excess reflects the dynasty's immense wealth. Filmed at Berlin's late-1960s modernist Congress Center, the circular residence required twenty-five vans of retro-modern furniture to fill it. The salon, decked in vibrant 1970s furnishings and Warhol-inspired art, showcases Plutarch's modern sensibilities, in stark contrast to the upstairs library inherited from his family. “We wanted to distinguish Plutarch from the dynasty he comes from,” Lawrence explains, reflecting on how the expansive volumes must be a facade of intellectual sophistication.

Recent findings suggest that the set decoration department spent weeks hand-folding and assembling thousands of hollow cardboard books, interspersed with real volumes, including a collection of Edgar Allan Poe’s poetry, which Plutarch references to Haymitch. “We imagined Plutarch might actually be the first Heavensbee to read some of those books,” Hanisch indicates. “He even says the library is one of the few worthwhile things his ancestors accomplished.”.

The library's custom-built curved bookshelves envelope the characters, symbolising the insularity of Capitol society. “Circles represent both inclusion and exclusion,” Hanisch says. “If you are in the circle, you're in. And if you're not, you're out.” As fans of the franchise will know, Plutarch (originally played by Philip Seymour Hoffman) later reveals himself as a double agent and leader of the underground rebellion against Snow’s regime.

The aspect ratio expands as Haymitch ascends into the eye-shaped arena, emphasizing the landscape’s immersive scale and beauty. While scouting locations, Lawrence drew inspiration from the dramatic landscapes in Terrence Malick’s A Hidden Life. “I had that in my head, only it was a little trippier. The Asturias were perfect,” he recalls. The kaleidoscopic design also inspired the official logo of the 50th Hunger Games, extending the arena’s psychedelic imagery into the Capitol’s propaganda.

Sources indicate that the Quarter Quell arena, in particular, embodies the surreal, fantastical ethos of the 1970s that permeates the film, illustrating how the Capitol exploits beauty to disguise its underlying manipulation and brutality. “As I was reading with Suzanne, I noted there was an Alice in Wonderland-like element to it, which made me think of the song ‘White Rabbit,’ which made me think of the late ’60s, early ’70s,” Lawrence recalls. “That kind of broke something open for me.”.

According to recent reports, designed in the shape of an eye, the eight to ten mile arena serves as a metaphor for the Capitol's omnipresent surveillance. A golden Cornucopia forms its pupil; vibrant meadows its iris; and the surrounding mountain ranges its whites. In the book, Haymitch describes the especially lethal arena masquerading as an idyllic landscape as a “poisonous beauty of an arena.”.

It has been revealed that lawrence and Haymitch in the arena. The physical flowers were concentrated in the foreground, while visual effects extended the colorful landscape into the distance.

Seeking to capture as much natural landscape as possible, Hanisch and location manager Klaus große Darrelmann discovered a remote valley in Asturias, Spain, surrounded by the Cantabrian Mountains. Transforming the isolated valley into a psychedelic paradise proved an enormous undertaking.“The arena was our nemesis,” notes Hanisch, recalling how the production had to bring extensive resources to the remote terrain. “You can't even imagine how far away it was or how hard it was to get to.” Crews spent weeks individually installing hundreds of thousands of artificial flowers throughout the meadows and forests.

Despite the arena’s dreamlike beauty, water sources, flowers, and vegetation conceal deadly poisons. “It’s the most colorful and playful dystopia you’ll ever see,” producer Nina Jacobson says. Perhaps more than anywhere else in Panem, the arena encapsulates how the Capitol weaponizes the electric zeitgeist of the ‘70s as an instrument of control. “To have something so overwhelmingly beautiful and seductive but poisonous and deadly is very cruel,” Hanisch says. “That contradiction captures the mentality of Panem at this point in its history.”.

Tesla stops selling every Cybertruck except the $109,990 Cyberbeast

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (813 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek
